newsitem.title: UK: Cargill declines comment on AIC default charge.
newsitem.headline: Cargill declines comment on AIC default charge.

text.p: Cargill International SA declined immediate comment on a statement by AIC that Cargill had failed to take full delivery of gas oil in the first five day period of the November IPE futures contract, a Cargill trader said on Thursday.

"Basically the one you should contact is (the Cargill spokesperson) in Minneapolis. She will be the only one actually talking to journalists on this issue," the trader said by telephone, referring to Cargill's corporate headquarters in the United States.
An AIC spokesman earlier on Thursday said Cargill had failed to lift the required volume of gas oil during the first five-day window of the November 16-30 delivery period.
He said Cargill failed to lift about 40 percent of the volume from Antwerp and a further 15 to 20 percent of the volume from Amsterdam, and therefore appeared to be in default.
AIC has said Cargill was due to take delivery of 627,800 tonnes, of which a third each is due to be lifted in the three five-day periods, November 16-20, November 21-25 and November 26-30.

International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) chief executive Lynton Jones said on Wednesday the exchange was closely monitoring the delivery of the November gas oil futures contract to ensure performance by the dominant short and long.
